chunks: From him, from Hammad, from Hariz and Safwan, from Al-'Ala' (all) from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who came to him and said, 'Buy for me some goods, perhaps I will buy them from you for cash or on credit.' So the man bought them on his behalf. He said, 'There is no harm in it; he buys it from him after he has taken possession of it.'

key_terms.اِبْتَعْ: Buy for me / Purchase on behalf of
key_terms.لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ: There is no harm in it / It is permissible
key_terms.مِنْ أَجْلِهِ: On his behalf / For his sake

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy goods for someone else with the intent to resell them to them?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS), the scholar clarifies the mechanism of *bai' al-musta'min* (sale by the borrower/agent), confirming that a person who purchases goods on behalf of another is permitted to resell them once they have taken actual possession (*qabd*). This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on effective ownership and possession as the prerequisite for a valid resale, distinguishing it from speculative sales of what one does not yet own. The hadith is recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, a primary source for Twelver Shia fiqh, highlighting the practical application of contract law in commercial transactions.
